title: Finite non-Leibniz energy-product envelope is stable, but it does not imply spatial decay
question: Does the volume-uniform Q3 energy envelope close a finite non-Leibniz product topology, and does that topology by itself imply spatial boundary commutator decay?
method: Define the four finite half-power contexts M_(a,b)(A)=||K^a A K^(-b)||_infinity for K=diag(1,4,9,16).
Verify exact context insertion and submultiplicative product bounds in a SymPy primary lane and an independently implemented Fraction lane.
Verify both orientations of a unitary cyclic-shift bond, the G endpoint conjugation envelope, and the six-layer/N-step exponential consequence.
Test the spatial implication on K=I: a cyclic shift transports a local projector to distance three while preserving every energy seminorm and producing an order-one commutator.
Compile Lean R209 for the exact context-insertion, absolute-product and conjugation-factor identities; retain the QFT-to-TECT production firewall.
finding: Primary 37/37, independent 34/34, integrated 27/27 and Lean R209 pass. The finite non-Leibniz product envelope is an exact algebraic subgate under the declared matrix/common-core hypotheses: M_(a,b)(B*AB)<=G^(2a+2b)M_(a,b)(A), and six matching layers yield a volume-independent exp(6C T(a+b)) bound when G^2<=1+C delta. The K=I cyclic-shift fixture has zero initial distant commutator and unit transported commutator despite unchanged energy seminorms, so the envelope alone supplies no spatial decay.
decision_reason: This closes only the finite non-Leibniz energy-product algebra requested after EXP-001024 and proves an exact necessity witness for an independent spatial first-passage estimate. It does not close the actual Q3 first-passage product, boundary commutator decay, all-shape exhaustion Cauchy, common alpha or KMS route.

adversarial_review.check: The product theorem is exact only on the finite matrix/common-core fixture; no domain closure is inferred.
The induced infinity norm is an algebraic proxy and does not select the physical Q3 topology.
The cyclic shift preserves K=I seminorms and produces an order-one distant commutator.
Volume-uniform growth does not give exhaustion summability or generator identification.
No heat_root_incidence or A1/R-192 production map appears.

qft_interface.closed: Finite non-Leibniz energy-product stability and an exact separation of energy control from spatial locality.
qft_interface.open: Actual Q3 first-passage product, boundary commutator decay, all-shape exhaustion Cauchy, common alpha, KMS, ground/gap and continuum remain open.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: No canonical A1/R-192 production owner or heat_root_incidence field is supplied.

boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite algebraic/topological checkpoint only. It does not prove a thermodynamic dynamics, common-alpha KMS, ground state, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A, Pre-A or TECT production closure.
next_action: Use the finite product envelope only as an energy-side factor in an actual first-passage branch/repeat sum; prove or falsify the two-sided response estimate and record the exact obstruction if the resummation cannot be made spatially summable.
